about.text: I'm {given}. I don't have a trade yet. Mum says I will when I'm bigger.
{name}. I've been in {settlement} longer than the well.
{given}'s the name. I keep the {job}'s hours and the {job}'s worries.
I'm {given}! I'm the {job}, and I love it.

about.job.text: I build. Houses, walls, the odd bridge. Every block goes where the plan says.
The fields keep this town fed. I keep the fields.
I walk the woods and bring back timber. Plant two for every one I fell.
Stone's in my bones. I cut it from the hill.
Up before the gulls, out on the water.
Sheep, goats, the odd stubborn cow. They're good company.
I track game in the hills. Quiet work.
Tables, doors, carts, cradles. If it's wood, I make it.
Bricks, dressed stone, glass. The town's bones and skin.
Tools, nails, hinges, and the dies the mint strikes coin with.
Bread at dawn, pies by noon. I'm the reason this town smells so good.
Ale, cider, a little something stronger for winter.
I keep the inn. Beds for travellers and the best stories in town.
I keep the stall. Buy low, sell fair, that's my motto.
I strike the coin and keep the treasury. Every bit is accounted for.
I keep the watch. Nothing comes through that gate without me knowing.
I tend the altar and the people who come to it.
I read, I write, I remember. Somebody has to.
Letters, parcels, gossip. I carry them all between the towns.
Wool to thread, thread to cloth, cloth to coats.
No trade, these days. I keep the house and mind everyone's business.

about.spouse: My {spouse} and I have been together for years.

about.spouse.text: {spouse}? Oh, we argue like cats, but I'd be lost without them.
Have you met my {spouse}? The finest person in {settlement}.

about.children: Our little ones keep us busy: {children}.

about.children.text: {children}. Mine, all of them, and every one a handful.
